## Round 2 -- 2026-11-19T19:00Z (plan 01 C.3a: s2_covers)

- Scope: uncommitted diff adding BE `s2_covers(cell, polygon_wkt)` (approximate inverted-index predicate in
  `functions_geo_cell.cpp`), FE `S2Covers.java` + its registrations, and UT
  `GeoCellTest.S2CoversIndexIsSupersetOfStContains`.
- Agent / model: `code-review` / `gpt-6-astra`.  Result: 1 finding (MEDIUM), accepted and deferred to its
  own item, 0 rejected.

### 1. MEDIUM -- each cover range costs two broad one-sided BKD scans (`functions_geo_cell.cpp:181-202`)
- Evidence: `cell >= lo` and `cell <= hi` each match roughly half the segment, so R ranges over M rows
  produce >= R x M intermediate doc ids before the AND.  `skip_try = true` also turns off the stock bypass
  safeguard.  `RANGE_QUERY` is not a usable numeric BETWEEN on the BKD path today
  (`snii_bkd_query.h`: only EQUAL / LT / LE / GT / GE).  SNII has a two-bound `BkdReader::range()`.
- Measured on the cluster: correct results; warm 3x faster than the full scan; cold 575-1,816 ms
  (01.geo.index.reuse.md section 3).  Consistent with the finding.
- Decision: kept for C.3a, because it is correct and measured, and C.3a's test tool passes.  The fix is
  plan 01 C.4: a bounded per-range BKD query, i.e. a two-bound query type wired through
  `build_bkd_query_bounds`, or a direct `BkdReader::range` call.  It is not hidden in this diff, because it
  touches shared index code and needs its own audit.
- Verification of C.3a: ASAN BE UT `GeoCellTest*` 4/4 (index result is a superset of ST_Contains on
  9,491 fixture points x 3 polygons, row path == index path, every BKD query has skip_try); FE compile
  OK; cluster table above.
